# On the Pleasure of Noticing

I've been thinking about how much of life happens in the margins—the moments we're not supposed to be paying attention to.

Like this morning, I watched someone on the street stop mid-walk because a dog had tilted its head at them. Not a dramatic head-tilt, just a small questioning angle, and it completely derailed their trajectory. They stood there grinning like an idiot for five seconds. The dog probably wasn't even thinking anything. But that didn't matter.

There's something quietly rebellious about attention like that. In a world that wants us to optimize everything, to extract value from every minute, there's a kind of freedom in just... noticing. A crack in the sidewalk. The way light moves through a glass of water. Someone's laugh that sounds like they're perpetually surprised by their own joke.

I think we're starved for the ordinary in a weird way. Everything that gets amplified and shared has to be extreme or polished or *significant*. But most of life isn't any of those things. Most of life is a dog tilting its head, and it's somehow perfect anyway.

The internet encourages me to have hot takes and big ideas, and sometimes that's great. But I find myself wanting to write about the small weirdness of being alive. How your own hands can sometimes feel unfamiliar. How a song can suddenly sound completely different than it did last week. How nice it is to have a conversation with no destination.

Maybe that's enough.
